summary: Whatcom County lookout site: a 1920 camp, then an L-4 cab built in 1935 or 1936, removed or destroyed in 1968. A hiking trail reaches the site, with views of Mount Baker.

facts.status_note: Lookout gone. The cab was removed or destroyed in 1968, depending on the source; a hiking trail still reaches the former site

access.note: WTA describes a hiking trail to the site; parking needs an America the Beautiful Pass or a Northwest Forest Pass

visit.trail_note: 2.5 miles round trip; climbs about 600 feet in half a mile (WTA). Old trails from the Komo Kulshan and Baker Lake guard stations are historical only

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com give an L-4 cab built in 1936; Willhite says likely 1935, and Forest Lookouts and Willhite both record panoramas taken on September 6, 1935 (Willhite says from the cab's roof). The story gives both years and says the sources disagree.
Register and Forest Lookouts say removed in 1968; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1968. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Two sources date the L-4 cab to 1936 and two to 1935 (Willhite, with September 1935 panoramas); the story gives both and does not choose. Fate is also disputed (removed versus destroyed, both 1968). The WTA hike is the only current-day source; its trailhead coordinates (48.6746) match the brief's Whatcom point, but the editor should confirm WTA means this site. WTA calls the destination the 'former lookout tower', which conflicts with the cab description; the story uses the cab. The 1928 account is cited by both Forest Lookouts and Willhite as 'Six Twenty-Six' and was not checked against the original. The brief's access 'unknown' could be updated to public from the WTA trail; no closure was found. Brief elevation 1652 m matches the Register's 5,420 ft (1,652 m). Verification 2026-10-09: Willhite gives the panorama date only in photo captions (Looking Southeast, Southwest, North, September 6, 1935) and says 'in September' in its text; the evidence list now carries the captions. Story text unchanged.
